subject: Physics
cards: AQA-7408.EMF_OF_A_BATTERY

State what is meant by the emf (electromotive force) of a battery.

[1 mark]

• Amount of **chemical energy** transferred / converted to **electrical energy** for 1 C of charge (through the battery).
• OR
• Work done in moving 1 C of charge **whole way** round circuit
Also accept: (The emf is) the terminal pd (of the battery) when there is no current in the battery.
AQA-7408.ANTIPARTICLE

State what is meant by an antiparticle.

[2 marks]

• Particle with equal (rest) mass/energy
• but **opposite** charge/baryon number/lepton number
AQA-7408.PRINCIPLE_OF_MOMENTS

State the principle of moments.

[2 marks]

• The clockwise moment(s) equals the anticlockwise moment(s)
• Includes **all** the following
• (system must be) in equilibrium
• moments about the same point
• sum of the clockwise moments equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments.
AQA-7408.THRESHOLD_FREQUENCY

State what is meant by the threshold frequency of radiation in the photoelectric effect.

[2 marks]

• Idea that it is the minimum (photon) frequency needed
• for (photo)electron(s) to be emitted
AQA-7408.CENTRE_OF_MASS

State what is meant by the centre of mass.

[1 mark]

• EITHER
• the point through which (the line of action of) a force has no turning effect/causes no rotation/ no torque
• OR
• where the mass of the body can be considered to be concentrated
• OR where the weight can be considered to act
Not accepted: where mass can be considered to act
Ignore: reference to force of gravity
AQA-7408.RESONANCE

Explain what is meant by resonance.

[2 marks]

• Idea that (at resonance) frequency of forced vibrations equals natural/resonant frequency
• Idea that amplitude (of vibrations/oscillations) is at a maximum
Also accept: fully labelled graph of amplitude vs driving frequency with resonance frequency clearly labelled and an amplitude peak.
Also accept: ‘wave frequency’ for ‘driving frequency’
Ignore: references to phase
AQA-7408.TRANSVERSE_WAVE

State what is meant by a transverse wave.

[2 marks]

• Idea that the oscillations (of particles in the wave) are at right angles
• to the direction of energy transfer
Also accept: ‘oscillates’ for ‘oscillations’
Also accept: ‘displacement’ for ‘oscillations’
Also accept: a correctly labelled diagram
Not accepted: ‘vibrations’
Not accepted: direction of (wave) motion/travel
Not accepted: a contradiction in 1
Ignore: Treat any reference to polarisation as neutral
Note: If no other mark given: award max 1 when answer suggests that amplitude is perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
AQA-7408.IONISATION

State what is meant by ionisation.

[1 mark]
Ionisation is the removal (or addition) of electrons from (to) an atom or molecule
AQA-7408.SPECIFIC_LATENT_HEAT_OF_FUSION

Explain what is meant by specific latent heat of fusion.

[2 marks]

• Specific latent heat of fusion is the **energy** (required) to change 1 kg / unit mass of material from the solid state to the liquid state or melt/fuse
• Without a change of temperature or at the freezing/melting temperature/point
AQA-7408.ELECTRIC_FIELD_STRENGTH

Define the electric field strength at a point in an electric field.

[2 marks]

• (The electric field strength at a point) is the force per unit charge
• On a (small) **positive** charge (at that point) (only given if an attempt is made at the first mark)
Also accept: Unit charge can be replaced by coulomb
Not accepted: An equation is not sufficient unless the symbols are defined
Note: (Reference to a point is not needed as it is in the question but a reference to moving between points or other points can cancel a mark.)
Note: If “mass” appears in the answer, it must be a synonym for “object”
AQA-7408.LENZ_S_LAW

State Lenz’s law.

[1 mark]

The **direction** of the **induced emf** (when there is a change of flux linkage) is such that it will (try) **to oppose the change** (of flux) that is producing it
Ignore: reference to current if emf is given.
Note: A reference to emf is needed rather than induced current as this is dependent on a circuit
AQA-7408.INTERNAL_ENERGY_OF_A_GAS

State what is meant by the internal energy of a gas.

[2 marks]

• It is the **sum/total** of the (kinetic and potential) energies of the **particles/atoms/molecules** (that move at random in the gas)
• For reference to kinetic energy of the gas or molecules
Also accept: This is independent of the first mark provided energy of the gas is given in some form
Also accept: So here an average kinetic energy would be acceptable
Not accepted: an average or a rms energy
Not accepted: a vague reference to an energy of or in the gas
AQA-7408.GRAVITATIONAL_POTENTIAL

Define gravitational potential at a point.

[1 mark]

the work done/energy **required** in bringing **1 kg/unit** mass from infinity to the point
Not accepted: A test mass should not be taken to be a unit mass
Ignore: extra comments eg about charge.
AQA-7408.BINDING_ENERGY_OF_A_NUCLEUS

State what is meant by the binding energy of a nucleus.

[2 marks]

• Energy required/work done to separate the nucleus
• into its individual nucleons/protons and neutrons
• OR
• Energy given out when a nucleus is formed
• from its individual nucleons/protons and neutrons
Also accept: If no other marks are awarded, condone the idea that “binding energy is how much greater the rest energy/mass of the constituent nucleons is than that of the nucleus” for one mark.
Also accept: Alternative words may be used instead of ‘separate’ but when used they must convey the correct idea.
AQA-7408.INTERNAL_ENERGY_OF_AN_IDEAL_GAS

State what is meant by the internal energy of an ideal gas.

[1 mark]

total kinetic energy of the particles
Also accept: “molecules” or “atoms” for “particles”
Also accept: Kinetic energy will be taken to mean total kinetic energy
Not accepted: use of mean kinetic energy or reference to kinetic energy of a single particle.
Not accepted: any reference that implies there is potential energy or any other energy added to the kinetic energy.
AQA-7408.RANDOM_PARTICLE_MOTION

State what is meant by random particle motion.

[2 marks]

• There is a range of speeds / kinetic energies
• Idea of no preferred direction
Also accept: velocity for speed in MP1.
Also accept: v_x = v_y = v_z or similar for MP2
Not accepted: A reference to average speed is not enough for MP1
Ignore: references to Brownian motion and collisions.
Note: Must express the idea that all directions are equally likely not just that there is a range of directions
Note: Any suggestion that particles do not follow Newton’s laws, are not deterministic, or the motion is unpredictable, is incorrect and restricts to MAX 1
AQA-7408.NORMAL_ADJUSTMENT

State what is meant by normal adjustment when applied to an astronomical refracting telescope.

[1 mark]

Final image at infinity.
Also accept: the focal plane/point of the eyepiece and objective lenses are co-incident.
Also accept: ‘rays leaving eyepiece/entering eye are parallel’
Also accept: distance between lenses is fo + fe
Also accept: answers which describe how the telescope is set up with named lenses unless fo and fe are used
Note: If Fo and Fe are used they must be defined
AQA-7408.STANDARD_CANDLE

State what is meant by a standard candle.

[1 mark]

It has a known absolute magnitude.
Also accept: Other wordings are possible
Note: It must be clear that the candidate knows that it is the intrinsic power/brightness that must be known
AQA-7408.RAYLEIGH_CRITERION

Explain what is meant by the Rayleigh criterion.

[2 marks]

• Rayleigh criterion identifies the minimum subtended angle between two objects whose (images) can be resolved.
• (Minimum angle is when) the central maximum of (the diffraction pattern of light from) one object coincides with the first minimum of (the diffraction pattern) of the second object.
AQA-7408.RADIOISOTOPE

State what is meant by a radioisotope.

[1 mark]

Material with nuclei which are unstable / will decay / emits ionising / radiation.
Note: At least two of the descriptors
AQA-7408.SOUND_INTENSITY

Define sound intensity.

[1 mark]

• Power (of sound) per unit area
• OR
• Energy (of source) per unit area per second
Also accept: ‘per m2’ for ‘per unit area’
AQA-7408.THRESHOLD_OF_HEARING

State what is meant by the threshold of hearing for a person with good hearing.

[2 marks]

• the minimum intensity that (a normal) ear can hear
• at 1 kHz
Also accept: ‘power per m2 ‘ for ‘intensity’
Not accepted: ‘minimum sound intensity level’
Note: word definition required: data sheet value is neutral
AQA-7408.LAW_OF_CONSERVATION_OF_ANGULAR_MOMENTUM

State the law of conservation of angular momentum.

[1 mark]

The (total) **angular** momentum (of a system) remains constant provided no external **torque** acts (on the system)
Also accept: ‘is conserved’ for ‘is constant’
Also accept: ang momtm before equals/is same as ang momtm after OR initial ang momtm = final ang momtm
Also accept: Iω is constant if symbols explained
Not accepted: 'force' in place of 'torque'
AQA-7408.ADIABATIC_CHANGE

Explain what is meant by an adiabatic change.

[1 mark]

(A change in which there is) no energy/heat transfer to or from the gas/system
Also accept: no heat enters or leaves the system.
AQA-7408.FIRST_LAW_OF_THERMODYNAMICS_TERMS

The first law of thermodynamics can be expressed by the equation Q = ΔU + W. State the meaning of each term in this equation.

[2 marks]

• Q: energy transferred/supplied **to** system (by heating)
• ΔU: **increase** in internal energy (of system)
• W: work done **by** system
Also accept: ‘gas’ in place of ‘system’
Also accept: ‘heat energy supplied’ for Q
Not accepted: ‘heat supplied’ for Q
Not accepted: 'heat' in place of 'energy'
Not accepted: 'heat transferred' on its own
Not accepted: 'thermal energy' or 'heat energy' on its own.
AQA-7408.MOMENT_OF_INERTIA

State what is meant by the moment of inertia of an object about an axis.

[1 mark]

Sum of all constituent masses × their radius/distance from the axis squared
Also accept: Σmr2 with m defined as small mass or constituent mass or particle at a radius r and Σ explained
Also accept: 'from the axis' missing
Also accept: a quantity expressing a body's tendency to resist angular acceleration/change in angular speed
AQA-7408.BLACK_BODY_RADIATION

State what is meant by black-body radiation.

[2 marks]

• Electromagnetic/EM radiation
• Spectrum with peak depending on temperature (of emitter alone).
Also accept: If no other mark awarded, allow 1 mark for (EM) radiation given off by perfect absorber /emitter.
Also accept: light for radiation
AQA-7408.INERTIAL_FRAME_OF_REFERENCE

State what is meant by an inertial frame of reference.

[1 mark]

One which moves at constant velocity
Also accept: a reference frame in which Newton’s laws / Newton’s first law holds.
AQA-7408.VIRTUAL_EARTH

Explain what is meant by a virtual earth.

[1 mark]

A virtual earth is a point that sits at 0 V (due to the configuration of the circuit) even though there is no direct physical connection to ground
Also accept: the idea that it acts as if grounded.
AQA-7408.AMPLITUDE_MODULATION

Describe what is meant by amplitude modulation (AM).

[1 mark]

amplitude of carrier varies in phase with information/audio signal
Also accept: labelled diagram in support
AQA-7408.R_3_10_2_EQUAL_LOUDNESS_CURVE_PROCEDURE

Describe the procedure used to gather the data for an equal loudness curve.

[2 marks]

• (different) frequencies are played (through earphones) and compared to a 1kHz reference signal
• Volume is changed until it sounds the same loudness as the reference signal
AQA-7408.R_3_10_2_LOUD_SOUND_HEARING_CHANGES

Describe the changes to a person’s hearing that may result from prolonged exposure to sound at 110 dB.

[2 marks]

• Idea of reduction in sensitivity at all frequencies
• Most loss occurs at 4 kHz
Also accept: for idea of reduction in sensitivity: hearing loss/ perceives sounds to be quieter/ drop in perceived loudness/ higher intensity required for same loudness
Also accept: a range of ±1 kHz provided that 4 kHz lies in the range
Not accepted: any suggestion that this is due to the loud noise being at 4 kHz
Note: If no other mark given award 1 mark for suggestion that person will suffer from tinnitus
AQA-7408.R_3_10_2_OSSICLES_ROLE

A sound wave produces a maximum increase in pressure on an ear of 2.5 × 10^-3 N m^-2. This causes a maximum increase in pressure in the fluid of the inner ear of 5.0 × 10^-2 N m^-2. Explain how the ossicles contribute to this increase in pressure in the fluid of the inner ear.

[2 marks]

• Ossicles act like levers
• To increase the force
AQA-7408.R_3_10_6_BIOLOGICAL_HALF_LIFE

Fluorine-18 has a biological half-life of 6.0 hours. Explain what is meant by this statement.

[2 marks]

• the time taken to halve the amount of fluorine-18/ number of particles is 6 hours
• by excretion of fluorine-18 from the body (by biological means)
Also accept: ‘mass’ as alternative to ‘amount’.
Also accept: ‘activity’
Not accepted: decay in MP1 or in MP2
AQA-7408.R_3_10_6_FLUORINE_18_DECAY_PARTICLES

Name the particles emitted when a fluorine-18 nucleus decays.

[1 mark]

Beta plus/positron and (electron) neutrino
Not accepted: emission of anti-neutrino, gamma, protons, neutrons or daughter nucleus scores zero.
Ignore: (incorrect) symbols.
AQA-7408.R_3_10_6_TECHNETIUM_GAMMA_TRACER

A hospital uses the radioactive isotope technetium-99m as a tracer. Technetium-99m emits only gamma rays. Explain why this makes technetium-99m suitable for use as a tracer.

[4 marks]

• Other radiation causes damage to tissue without being detectable
• Pass through the body (tissue) so that it can be detected (outside)
• Least ionising so that it causes least damage to tissue
• Energy / frequency of gamma is similar to medical X-rays so that an X-ray camera can be used for detection
Not accepted: Reference to least ionising without reason not enough
AQA-7408.R_3_12_2_ULTRAVIOLET_CATASTROPHE_PROPOSAL

In the early 1900s a contradiction between experimental results and theoretical predictions was termed the ultraviolet catastrophe. A proposal was made that allowed a resolution of the contradiction. Outline this proposal.

[1 mark]

Light (waves) / (EM) radiation (is emitted) in **quanta** and idea that energy is proportional to frequency
Also accept: small packets of energy/waves for quanta.
Also accept: energy for EM radiation.
Not accepted: photons / particles.
AQA-7408.R_3_13_1_MOSFET_LOW_POWER_PROPERTY

MOSFETs are commonly used in circuits where low power consumption is important to extend battery life. State and explain the property of MOSFET devices that makes them useful in these circuits.

[2 marks]

• High input resistance
• low/no energy consumption when in the ON and OFF states
• OR
• No input current/control by pd only.
AQA-7408.R_3_13_5_JOHNSON_VS_BCD_COUNTER

A Johnson decade counter uses a Johnson counter together with decoding logic. This arrangement produces a single logic 1 at a series of outputs Q0-Q9 in a continuous sequence. Describe one functional difference and one functional similarity between how a Johnson decade counter and a BCD counter output their counts.

[2 marks]

• **Difference:** BCD counter outputs binary codes. A Johnson decade counter outputs a single output sequentially
• **Similarity:** Both counters recycle at the 10th pulse
Also accept: max counter value for 10th pulse.
Also accept: both counters count from 0-9
Also accept: both counters count to 10
AQA-7408.R_3_13_6_CARRIER_WAVE

State what is meant by a carrier wave within a radio transmission system. Go on to explain how the carrier wave is used in this system.

[2 marks]

• A carrier wave is a fixed frequency (radio wave assigned to a radio station and used to transmit information/signal)
• Some aspect of the carrier wave characteristic (eg amplitude / frequency) must be varied / modulated (to represent the information / signal being transmitted)
AQA-7408.R_3_13_6_ELECTRICAL_NOISE_EFFECTS

Describe the effect that electrical noise can have:
on the signal and
on the communication system.

[2 marks]

Effect of electrical noise on the signal:
• degrades the quality of the signal
Effect of electrical noise on the communication system:
• reduces the efficiency of the transmission e.g. increased latency of the system
AQA-7408.R_3_13_6_ELECTRICAL_NOISE_ORIGIN

Electrical noise can affect communication systems. Describe one origin of electrical noise in a communication system.

[1 mark]

Internal noise:
• thermal agitation of electrons / charge carriers in a conductor
• OR
External noise:
• idea of electromagnetic interference (EMI) eg cross-talk / power switching etc.
Also accept: one example for the mark
AQA-7408.R_3_2_1_ANTINEUTRINO_IN_BETA_MINUS

Explain why an electron antineutrino, rather than an electron neutrino, is produced during β- decay.

[2 marks]

• (It must be an electron antineutrino to) conserve lepton number
• An electron and (electron) antineutrino have lepton numbers of opposite signs.
• Or
• An electron and (electron) antineutrino have a (total) lepton number of zero.
• **Alternative:**
• Producing an (electron) neutrino wouldn’t conserve lepton number
• An electron and (electron) neutrino have lepton numbers of the same sign.
• Or
• An electron and (electron) neutrino have a (total) lepton number equal to 2.
Also accept: Appropriate particle equation seen annotated with correct lepton numbers.
AQA-7408.R_3_2_1_SPECIFIC_CHARGE_HYDROGEN_3

Hydrogen has three naturally occurring isotopes. One of these isotopes is hydrogen-3. The specific charge of the hydrogen-3 nucleus is less than the specific charges of the nuclei of the other two isotopes. Suggest why.

[2 marks]

• Idea that nuclei of the hydrogen isotopes have same charge / same number of protons (as hydrogen-3)
• Idea that nuclei of other isotopes have less mass / fewer nucleons / fewer neutrons (than hydrogen-3)
Also accept: correct comparison of hydrogen-3 with either hydrogen-2 or hydrogen-1
Also accept: reverse argument
Not accepted: incorrect statements about numbers of neutrons or protons as reason for lighter nuclei.
AQA-7408.R_3_2_1_LARGE_INTERNATIONAL_TEAMS

The discovery of particles such as the λ0 is made by large international research teams. Suggest one reason for this.

[1 mark]

• Any **one** from
(teams must be large and international) because:
• research is expensive / requires funding from many countries
• both scientists and engineers are required (because the machines used for research are complex/large pieces of civil engineering)
• research is multi-faceted / multi-disciplinary (because computation/theory/ etc. is required)
• research is round-the-clock (so teams are large to work on shift basis)
• they are needed to process the large amounts of data produced
Not accepted: idea that it ‘avoids bias’ or ‘reproducibility’.
Ignore: Treat idea of peer review as neutral (this argues for independent teams).
AQA-7408.R_3_2_2_SCINTILLATOR_PHOTON_PRODUCTION

Scintillation counters are used to detect beta particles. A scintillation counter consists of a scintillation material and a photomultiplier tube (PMT). Beta particles collide with atoms in the scintillation material, which emits photons of light as a result. Explain how photons are produced by collisions between beta particles and atoms.

[2 marks]

• Idea that atoms gains energy (from beta particle) eg atoms excited or atoms/electrons moved to higher energy levels
• Idea that atom loses energy by emission of light/photons eg atoms de-excite or electrons move to lower energy levels
Also accept: ionisation as named process
AQA-7408.R_3_3_1_MICROWAVES_VS_SOUND_DIFFERENCES

Microwaves and sound waves travel at different speeds. Describe two other differences between microwaves and sound waves.

[2 marks]
AQA-7408.R_3_6_2_KINETIC_THEORY_ASSUMPTIONS

In the kinetic theory model, it is assumed that there are many identical particles moving at random. State two other assumptions made in deriving the equation pV = (1/3) N m (c_rms)^2.

[2 marks]

• Any two from
• Volume of molecules/particles is negligible/small compared to the volume of the container
• Collision time is negligible/small compared to the time between collisions
• Collisions are elastic or kinetic energy is conserved
• There are negligible/no forces between molecules/particles except during collisions
Also accept: missing reference to “except during collisions” in bullet 4.
Also accept: “Newtonian mechanics apply”
Not accepted: Reference to the volume occupied by the gas must be clear for the first point. So ‘volume of gas’ is not enough.
AQA-7408.R_3_8_1_GAMMA_STERILISATION_REASON

Suggest, with a reason, which type of radiation is likely to be the most appropriate for the sterilisation of metallic surgical instruments.

[1 mark]

• γ radiation because it is very / the most penetrating
• OR
• γ radiation because it is penetrating enough to irradiate all sides of the instruments.
• OR
• γ radiation is penetrating so instruments can be sterilised without removing the packaging.
Not accepted: It is not sufficient to just state ‘gamma’
Note: The quoted radiation must be gamma only and not a mixture
Note: The mark is based on the reason for the choice
AQA-7408.R_3_8_1_NEUTRONS_IN_THERMAL_REACTOR

A thermal nuclear reactor uses enriched uranium as its fuel. This is fuel in which the ratio of U-235 to U-238 has been artificially increased from that found in naturally-occurring ore. Describe what happens when neutrons interact with U-235 and U-238 nuclei in a thermal nuclear reactor.

[3 marks]

• U-235 (absorbs) a neutron with added information
• U-235/6 then divides/splits and gives out more neutrons
• U-238 absorbs/scatters **neutrons**
Also accept: To become U-236
Also accept: absorbs a slow moving neutron
Also accept: absorbs a thermal neutron
Note: If no marks awarded but the first two marking points are made without identifying the isotope give one mark
Note: If the answer implies that U-238 in any way is involved in fission this mark is lost
AQA-7408.R_3_9_1_CCD_ADVANTAGES_OVER_EYE

One advantage of using a CCD with a telescope is that the data can be stored and processed on a computer. Explain two other advantages of using a CCD rather than the eye when making an observation with a telescope.

[2 marks]

Two from:
• Better quantum efficiency and therefore more (of the incident) light/photons detected (per second)
• Pixels smaller than rods/cones/retinal cells therefore better resolution
• Detects light outside visible spectrum so more information / more (of the incident) light detected with CCD
• Longer exposure (time) possible so more light/photons detected
Note: If no other marks given: award MAX 1 for two features / two advantages without explanation
AQA-7408.R_3_9_3_ACTIVE_BLACK_HOLE_OBSERVATION

Astronomers believe that M87 has an active supermassive black hole at its centre. Suggest one observation that leads to this conclusion.

[1 mark]

One from:
• (idea of) very intense radio-wave emitter
• bright X-ray source
Also accept: ‘quasar’ or description of quasar
Also accept: “jets” of (sources of) electromagnetic radiation
Not accepted: ‘γ-ray burst’
AQA-7408.R_3_9_3_QUASAR_STOPS_EMITTING

IC2497 is a galaxy that contained a quasar. It is believed that the quasar stopped emitting radiation several thousand years ago. Suggest why the quasar stopped emitting radiation.

[2 marks]

• Quasars are formed around black holes
• **Black hole** (at the centre of IC2497) no longer has matter falling into it
Also accept: black hole no longer feeding;
Also accept: Black hole no longer active.
Note: If no mention of black holes no marks can be awarded.
AQA-7408.R_3_1_2_VERNIER_CALLIPERS_PUTTY_PROBLEM

Conductive putty can easily be formed into different shapes to investigate the effect of shape on electrical resistance. A student uses vernier callipers to measure the diameter d of a uniform cylinder made of the putty. Suggest one problem with using callipers to make this measurement.

[1 mark]

callipers may **reduce** the (reading of the) diameter
Also accept: the idea that the callipers may ‘distort’ / ‘deform’ / ‘push in’ the putty, eg ‘change the shape’ / ‘crush’ / ‘squash’ / ‘cut into’ / ‘squeeze’
Not accepted: implication that density could change, eg ‘volume will change’ / ‘will compress’;
Not accepted: ‘putty will move’ / ‘not able to grip the putty hard enough’
Ignore: ‘change reading’ / ‘give incorrect reading’
AQA-7408.R_3_10_1_HYPERMETROPIA_UNAIDED_EYE

A person suffers from hypermetropia (long sight). Use of a spectacle lens of power +2.0 D allows the person to just see clearly an object placed 24 cm away from the eye. Explain why the unaided defective eye cannot form a clearly focused image of the object placed 24 cm from the eye.

[2 marks]

• Eye lens cannot be made powerful enough / rays cannot be bent enough / eyeball is too short
• cannot be brought to a focus on the retina / fovea / back of the eyeball
Also accept: not strong / fat/convex enough
Also accept: rays would be / are focused behind the retina
Not accepted: fat enough - neutral answer
AQA-7408.R_3_10_1_MYOPIA_FAR_POINT

A human eye has a far point of 6.0 m. State the name of this defect of vision.

[1 mark]

myopia
Also accept: short sightedness
AQA-7408.R_3_10_5_FOCAL_SPOT_SIZE

X-rays originate from a region on the rotating anode known as the focal spot. Explain:
- one advantage of using a small focal spot
- why the focal spot should not be too small.

[2 marks]

• (small size of focal spot) to increase sharpness of image
• Idea of (must not be too small otherwise) danger of overheating (the anode)
Also accept: to reduce (size of) penumbra / reduce region of geometric unsharpness
Also accept: improve (spatial) resolution
Also accept: see finer detail
Also accept: reduce blurring at edges (of image)
Also accept: to limit temperature increase (of anode)
Also accept: to prevent it heating up too quickly
Ignore: more precise beam / more accurate beam
Ignore: clearer image / better image
Ignore: better focused
AQA-7408.R_3_12_1_CROOKES_CATHODE_RAYS_PARTICLES

When a large potential difference is applied between the cathode and anode the paddle wheel is seen to rotate and travel along the rail towards the anode. Explain how this experiment led Crookes to conclude that cathode rays are particles and that these particles caused the movement of the paddle.

[2 marks]

• Cathode rays/electrons move from cathode toward anode
• The paddle wheel has gained energy from cathode rays/electrons.
Also accept: move left to right
Also accept: as alternatives for energy kinetic, energy/momentum/impulse
Ignore: references to force.
Ignore: references to applying a magnetic field.
AQA-7408.R_3_12_1_THOMSON_SPECIFIC_CHARGE_SIGNIFICANCE

This question is about Thomson's determination of the electron's specific charge. Explain the significance of the result of Thomson's determination.

[2 marks]

• Specific charge was **much** larger / approx. 2000 times than the largest so far discovered / hydrogen ion / hydrogen nucleus / proton
• Electron has a **much** smaller mass than the hydrogen ion (proton)
Also accept: << and/or >> but not < or >
Not accepted: references to hydrogen atom or just hydrogen in 1 but condone in 2
Not accepted: larger in mp1 and smaller in mp2 is not sufficient without much/very/…
Ignore: references to size.
Ignore: "or greater charge"
Note: A comparison is required in 1 and 2
AQA-7408.R_3_10_3_ECG_PAD_BACKING_GEL

A backing gel is used between an ECG pad and the skin of the patient. The gel is sticky. This property ensures that the pad is securely attached to the skin. Explain:
- one other reason why the backing gel is needed
- one other property of the backing gel
- how the skin is prepared for the pad to be applied.

[3 marks]

**Why backing is needed**:
• Idea that gels improves electrical contact
**Property of backing**:
• gel should have low (electrical) resistance or
• non-irritating to skin or
• shouldn't react to chemicals produced by skin
**How skin is prepared**:
• skin is shaved / rubbed with abrasive paper/ hair removed
Also accept: skin is dried or cleaned
Not accepted: reference to or implication of acoustic resistance / impedance
AQA-7408.R_3_13_2_PCM_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY

Pulse code modulation (PCM) is used to encode live music as an uncompressed digital audio file. Sampling of the analogue signal is carried out at 44.1 kHz. A 16-bit system is used to encode each of the two channels that make up the stereo signal. Explain why the sampling frequency used is suitable for this task.

[2 marks]

• Audio range (bandwidth) is 20 kHz
• The sampling frequency should be at least **twice** the maximum frequency / bandwidth
Note: Reference to Nyquist theorem without reference to numerical data - 1 mark only
AQA-7408.R_3_3_2_TIR_LASER_IN_WATER_STREAM
